items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We never played behind Hazel when she did her act, but one time I suppose she wanted to see what quality the band really had because she made an arrangement on a song that she wanted us to accompany her [on]...

ctx.x: Another act was called the Golden Gate Quartet. Their names were Bill Johnson, Clyde Redick, Wilson and . They had a style of singing gospel songs which I had never heard before. In fact I didn't know anything about gospel singing except what I had heard in Baptist churches. But this was more like Holy-Holy singing to me, because it had a jazz rhythm and these fellows slap their thighs with their hands in four-four rhythm; and Yank accompanied them on drums with wire brushes on the snare drum and the joint kept…

The other act was a young woman named Hazel Scott. Hazel was a classical pianist who would play a classical number as it was supposed to be played, and then do the same number in jazz. She was well trained and was also an arranger and jazz singer. Yank also accompanied her with wire brushes. In fact he played only wire brushes which sometime didn't give the band the push it needed on certain numbers.

We didn't play loud because it was not necessary. Teddy had a soft when touch on piano, Benny Morton was at his best/playing not too loud and so was I. That was the big difference in playing in a big band and a small combo. In a big band you must blow loud and my ideas and technique were not as good when I had to play loud.
